title: The CAP theorem, and choosing between consistency and availability

videos.script: Keep two copies of your data on two machines, and sooner or later the network between them breaks. {{copies}} At that moment each machine has to decide what to do with a write it cannot pass on. {{moment}} It can refuse, and stay correct. Or it can accept, and stay available, knowing the other copy is now wrong. {{choice}} That is the CAP theorem, and it is less dramatic and more useful than its reputation. {{reputation}} On your machine you will run two PostgreSQL servers, one copying the other, and cut the cable between them. {{lab}} With synchronous replication the primary refuses to finish a write it cannot copy, and your client waits. {{cp}} With asynchronous replication the write goes through at once, and the copy keeps answering with yesterday's number. {{ap}} Then the part people miss: when nothing is broken, the same choice is still being made, between waiting and being right. {{pacelc}} At the end you will choose, operation by operation, for Quitanda. The cart and the payment do not want the same answer.
